newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends limit-up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends limit-up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly limit-up in active trading on Monday due to last Friday's heavy gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended limit-up at 20,050 yuan ($2,415) per tonne, rising 500 yuan. It opened at limit-up and hit an intra-day low of 19,950.
December rose 480 to 19,780, January 530 to 20,060, March 500 to 20,060, April 480 to 20,040 and May 530 to 20,030.
Combined volume rose sharply to 136,660 tonnes from 45,680.
Copper opened mostly limit-up and stayed at that level for most of the session.
Traders said LME's large gains triggered heavy stop-loss buying and further rises were likely in the next few days.
"Panic stop-loss buying was responsible for today's rises and heavy volume indicated that many investors were optimistic about the future market trend," one trader said.
"Most contracts held above the key 20,000-yuan resistance level, which suggests that copper is likely to begin a new rebound," he added.
Traders said the confidence of long position holders greatly improved after sharp rises today, with technical charts supporting furthers rises.
"Despite poor long- and mid-term fundamentals, investors believed the rebound will continue after breaching the 20,000-yuan level," a second trader said.
But traders said that some institutions were betting on the level of LME stockpiles to support futures prices.
Analysts expect copper to rise further in the next few days if the LME keeps going up.
Aluminium ended little changed in paper-thin trading. The December contract did not trade, January rose 80 to 13,480, February unchanged at 13,280.
Combined volume fell to 20 tonnes from 1,000.
